Implementation plan (writing this down before a context compaction, so it survives): ITEM 1 no-flood+prioritise — (a) bump Recite.turn_wait_ms and BargeIn.quiet_ms defaults from 1500 to 2500 (2.5s, within the 2-3s ask); keep them as two separate fields (existing tests assign r.barge.quiet_ms directly, e.g. lines ~93/137/201/296 of Recite.test.mjs — true unification into one field would break those; document as a deliberate, lower-risk choice, true merge left as a future simplification per the old review note). (b) 'direct answer plays first': from_wire() currently only acts on chat.from.id==='smart' (both the chat.from.kind==='assistant' branch and the line[*].replies.add branch), silently dropping any OTHER assistant id entirely today. New: add Recite.agent_update(text,id,from_id) for non-smart assistant lines — collapses to 'I have an update on {label}, tap to hear it.' via a new Recite.agent_label(from_id) static (strips mastermind-/minion-/reviewer-/clarity- prefix, dashes/underscores→spaces). If this.cue_pending is true (owner's line landed, no reply yet) the update is HELD in a new this.pending_updates=[] array (not queued), with a safety this.update_hold_timer (this.update_hold_ms=4000) that flushes it regardless if no smart reply ever arrives. this.flush_updates() (queue()s each held update via a new queue_update(text,id) helper that also calls mark_when_done) is called from from_wire() right AFTER this.final()/this.partial() complete for a smart reply (both call sites: the chat.from.kind==='assistant' branch and the replies.add branch, and the ev.kind==='stream' branch) — i.e. AFTER the smart reply's own chunks are queued, so ordering comes out 'direct answer first, update behind it'. If cue_pending is false when an update arrives, queue_update() runs immediately (no hold) since there's nothing to preempt. stop() must also clear pending_updates + the timer. Dedup/played-id tracking reuses this.done/mark_when_done exactly like final() does, keyed on the RAW text (not the collapsed label). ITEM 2 tap-to-pause — new file ReciteTap.js (Recite.Tap, instantiated in Recite's constructor like this.tap = new this.constructor.Tap({recite:this}), alongside barge/highlight), a bubble-phase (not capture) document click listener: ignores clicks inside `a, button, input, textarea, select, [role=button], [contenteditable]` (covers links, mention chips — ext/Mention's chip is an <a class=mention>—, and buttons) or inside ReciteHighlight.SKIP (the bar's own copy), only acts when the click lands inside ReciteHighlight.ROOTS (the same bubble-container selector the karaoke highlight already uses) and recite.chunks.length>0, then just calls recite.toggle() — a global play/pause, not per-bubble resume (arbitrary-bubble resume is item 3, explicitly deferred). No CSS hover affordance added this round (not asked for; left for item 4's bubble toolbar). Both pieces get Recite.test.mjs cases, readme.md Open-list items 1–2 removed/renumbered, and an architecture.md decision bullet each. answer.reply: Fixed both blocking items and all five smaller notes, commit e4cbff311: (1) flush_updates() now only runs when the stream itself ends (ev.text===''), not on every partial — a two-sentence stream test proves an update no longer lands mid-stream. findings.text: The review shots don't show the final page (Requirements 2, proof). The worktree's `page.js` (e4cbff311) swaps the long code comment for an on-page caption ("Tap the bubble below to pause or resume…"), but `shots/127-…-Recite/400.png` and `1920.png`, taken at 03:58 after that commit, still show the old three-line `// A real chat bubble…` comment in the code view and no caption. `shots/tap-to-pause-400.png` and `-1200.png` have no caption above the bubble either. The page that will land has never been shot. Re-shoot at 400 and 1200 from a fresh server load before `merge.mjs`. Most likely the worktree server was serving a cached `page.js`.

Spoken line: an agent update says "I have an update on X, tap to hear it", but tapping does not play that update yet (Words 11, Requirements 1c). It only pauses or resumes whatever is already playing. The readme's Open item 1 and `doc/architecture.md` both say so, and they name Resumable bubbles as the fix. The wording is the owner's, so it stays. Until Resumable bubbles lands, the owner will hear a promise that does nothing.

The direct answer plays first only among held agent updates (Requirements 1b). `final()` still queues behind anything already queued, including an earlier `smart` reply or an update queued before the owner's line. "Plays first" holds only for updates that arrive while `cue_pending` is true. This is reasonable, but the readme doesn't say where the guarantee stops.

`ReciteTap` is a new class, and nothing shows it live: it is not `track()`ed, unlike `Recite` (rules: show the class and its live instances). It holds almost no state (`recite`, `handler`), so this is a note.

`ReciteTap.click()` backs off whenever *any* selection exists on the page (`getSelection().toString()`), not only one inside the tapped bubble. If the owner leaves a word selected anywhere else, every bubble tap does nothing until they click elsewhere. Checking that the selection's anchor sits inside the bubble would narrow it.

The new tap-to-pause bullet in `doc/architecture.md` runs about 330 words in one paragraph (content 3). It covers four topics in one block: the toggle, the drag guard, the unkept "tap to hear it" promise, and listener lifetime. Split it into sub-bullets, the way the echo decision above it is split.
`ReciteTap.IGNORE`'s comment says "the bar's own copy", but the bar's copy is handled by `ReciteHighlight.SKIP` on the next line, not by `IGNORE`. The comment is slightly wrong.

findings.text: No-flood treats every assistant id except `smart` as an agent update, and the real wire carries other ids (Requirements 1c). `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1537` posts the fast seat's replies as `from: {kind:"assistant", id:"fast"}`. `ux/Dictate/Dictate.js:737` (`log_revision`) posts each voice revision of the owner's own line as `id:"revise"`, and `AISessionConversation.js:91` uses `id: c.by ?? "card"`. These lines used to be dropped silently. Now each one speaks "I have an update on fast / revise, tap to hear it." `revise` lands on every dictated sentence, so this adds a spoken line per utterance, which is the flood the ask set out to stop. Fix: name what counts as an agent update (an allow-list, or `from.agent` set and the id not a seat role), skip `fast`/`revise`, and add a test that feeds a `revise` line and a `fast` line and expects nothing queued.

On the demo, the bubble does nothing until something is playing (Words, Flow). `ReciteTap.click()` returns early when `recite.chunks` is empty. The caption "Tap the bubble below to pause or resume" doesn't say to press Read it aloud first, so a first tap looks broken. The bubble also repeats the textarea text right above it (shots/tap-to-pause-1200.png, middle band), so the same paragraph shows twice.

Tap to pause also fires on the owner's own bubbles. `ReciteHighlight.ROOTS` is the whole thread container (`.ux-dictate-widget-thread`, `.chat-v3`), so tapping any line in the thread toggles playback, not only taps on replies. The ask says "tapping a bubble", so this is probably fine, but neither doc says it.

The "direct answer first" promise only holds for updates that arrive while `cue_pending` is true. The readme now says so (the No flood paragraph), so the last review's note is answered. Item 1 would make this matter more: as built, a `fast` reply would hold the smart answer's queue slot.

answer.reply: Fixed the real bug, commit 3c88f6390: from_wire() now only treats a reply as an agent update when from.id matches Recite.AGENT_ID (mastermind-/minion-/reviewer-/clarity- prefixes, the same ones agent_label() already stripped) — 'fast', 'revise' and 'card' fall through to the old silent drop, exactly as before this task. revise posts on every dictated sentence, so this was a real flood regression; new test proves all three are ignored (30/30 now). Notes: page.js's caption now says to press Read it aloud first; architecture.md documents that ReciteHighlight.ROOTS covers the whole thread (owner's own lines included) and that the 'plays first' guarantee only covers held updates. Re-shot both paused-bubble screenshots again for the caption wording change, verified the new text is live in the DOM first. Re-running review.mjs.

findings.text: The readme still says every non-smart assistant reply is an agent update. Commit 3c88f6390 narrowed this to `Recite.AGENT_ID` ids (mastermind-/minion-/reviewer-/clarity-), but the readme's **No flood** paragraph opens "a reply from any assistant but the smart one is an agent update". A fresh agent reading only the readme would expect `fast`/`revise` to speak. The same stale wording is in the `pending_updates` field comment (`Recite.js:54`, "a reply from any assistant id but \"smart\"") and the test-block comment (`Recite.test.mjs:210`). `doc/architecture.md:15` (the turn-taking decision) still says `turn_wait_ms` (1.5 s). The default is now 2.5 s (`Recite.js:43`, and the same doc's own "No flood, piece 1" bullet). Update the number, or point that line at piece 1.

`check_wait()` still falls back to `this.turn_wait_ms ?? 1500` (`Recite.js:164`), the old default. It is harmless because the field is always set, but it reads as a second default that disagrees with the first. Use 2500, or drop the fallback.
